The whole of [Rhythm](elements-rhythm.qmd) on one sheet. Every ▶ plays the example. Tick **British note names** for crotchets and quavers. Press **Full screen** to put the sheet on the whole screen for
revision or for the class board.

## The sheet

::::::: {.el-sheet .column-page data-title="Rhythm: note lengths and speed"}
:::::: {.el-grid}

::::: {.el-card}
#### Note lengths
<p>In beats: [whole note]{.nn} 4 · [half note]{.nn} 2 · [quarter note]{.nn} 1 · [eighth note]{.nn} ½ · [sixteenth note]{.nn} ¼.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="80"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/16
K:C
c8 c4 c2c2|cccc cccc c4 z4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Rests
<p>Every note length has a matching rest: a silence of the same length.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="80"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/16
K:C
c4 z4 c2 z2 c z c z|c8 z8|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Dots
<p>A dot adds half the note's value again: a dotted [half note]{.nn} is 3 beats, a dotted [quarter note]{.nn} 1½.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="90"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:G
G6 B2|d3 c B2 A2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Ties
<p>Joins two notes of the same pitch into one longer note, often across a [measure]{.nn} line.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="90"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:G
G4- G2 A2|B8|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Triplets
<p>Three notes played evenly in the time of two, marked 3.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="90"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:G
(3BcB (3AGA G4|(3GAB (3cde d4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Syncopation
<p>The accent <strong>off</strong> the beat, often a note tied over the strong beat. Pop, funk, Latin, jazz.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
c2 c c- c2 c2|z G G2- G4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### [Fermata]{.nn}
<p>Hold the note longer than written; the pulse waits.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="90"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:F
F A c A|!fermata!G4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Tempo words
<p>BPM = beats per minute. A rough guide:</p><ul>
<li><strong>Lento, adagio</strong>: slow, under 70</li>
<li><strong>Andante</strong>: walking pace, 75–100</li>
<li><strong>Moderato</strong>: moderate, 100–120</li>
<li><strong>Allegro</strong>: fast, 120–160</li>
<li><strong>Vivace, presto</strong>: very fast, 160+</li></ul>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Changing tempo
<p><strong>Accelerando</strong>: getting faster. <strong>Ritardando / rallentando</strong>: slower. <strong>A tempo</strong>: back to speed. <strong>Rubato</strong>: stretching the tempo for expression.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
Q:1/4=80
K:C
"^accel."C E G E|[Q:1/4=112]C E G E|[Q:1/4=140]"^rit."C E G E|[Q:1/4=100]C E G E|[Q:1/4=70]C4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card .el-wide}
#### Check yourself
<div class="eq" data-set="rhythm"></div>
:::::

::::::
:::::::

## Describing rhythm and tempo

- Name the tempo with a word *and* a rough BPM, then any changes: "allegro, about 140 BPM, with a ritardando at the end".
- To find a tempo by ear, tap along: the [Tap Along](../tools/tap-along.qmd) tool counts it for you.

- The longer lesson, with fuller examples: [Elements 7: Rhythm and Tempo](elements-rhythm.qmd).
